reading.title: Words That Mean Two Things
reading.purpose: Hear how one word can have two meanings.
paras: Some words have two meanings. Bark is on a tree, and a dog makes a bark. A bank holds money, and a river has a bank. You wave hello, and the sea has a wave.
Spring is a season, and a spring can bounce. A bat can fly, and a bat can hit a ball. You rock a baby, and you pick up a rock. A seal can swim, and you can seal a letter.

qs.q: A river has a bank. What is a bank here?
choices: The land along the side of the river.
qs.why: For a river, a bank is the land along its side.

qs.q: Which word can name a season or a coil that bounces?
qs.why: The reading says spring is a season, and a spring can bounce.

qs.q: What does it mean to seal a letter?
qs.why: A seal can swim, but to seal a letter means to close it tightly.

needsReview.reason: A list-like text about two-meaning words; the lesson needs it, but a teacher may prefer to read it with pictures.
